Sasha: Heads-up — onboarding Magnet-14B int4 on dev-stack shows a subtle divergence when context > ~16k tokens. Repro attached below, seen on both rook & shard runtimes. @Maya can you take a look?

Maya: Ok saw it briefly in the staging trace this morning. Short description: generation stream is identical until ~14k tokens then tokens start shifting (off-by-one insertions) and KV indices show an unexpected wrap. :thinking_face:

Liam: I ran a local bisect. Disabling the rope-scaling heuristic removes the shift (i.e., set rope_scale=1.0), but perf degrades. Might be an interaction between rope rescaling and int4 packing alignment.

Sasha: Repro commands I used (dev image):
```bash
# reproduce longctx run (dev cluster)
python -m redwood.tests.longctx_repro \  --model magnet-14b-int4 \  --seq_len 32000 \  --rope_scale auto \  --kv_handshake enabled \  --batch 1
```

Sasha: Minimal log excerpt (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-22 08:12:03] kv_handshake: priming keys 0..2047
[2026-03-22 08:12:03] rope: applied scale=0.9987 (auto)
[2026-03-22 08:12:45] kv:index: write pos=16383 shard=2
[2026-03-22 08:12:45] kv:index: write pos=16384 shard=2  <-- unexpected boundary
[2026-03-22 08:12:46] gen: token_shift_detected at tok=14012 delta=+1
```

Anita: I kicked off an AB eval against our longprefill goldset (1k examples, varied lengths). Initial numbers: int4 w/rope_auto has MRR ~ -3.1% vs f16 baseline at 20k context, perplexity +0.6. Not huge but consistent.

eval-bot: Eval run 2026-03-22 09:40: completed. Summary: samples=1000, avg_ppl_f16=11.2, avg_ppl_int4=11.8, mrr_drop=3.1% @20k. Full CSV uploaded to <https://internal-redwood/reports/5467890123|report>. :memo:

Maya: Hypothesis: int4 layout causes padding so KV rows shift at certain write offsets; rope rescale multiplies index math so the handshake expects different alignment. Could be off-by-one in the shard boundary when compressed wordsize != 4. Will try forcing 32-byte alignment and re-run.

Liam: Quick test: disabled continuous batching and forced aligned prefill -> divergence gone. CPU cost up ~6% but suggests runtime alignment bug. Patch proposal: ensure kv_write_pos uses padded_stride = round_up(bytes_per_key, 32) before modulo operations. I put a draft in PR: <https://git.internal/rw/infra/pulls/1234|pr#1234>. :eyes:

Sasha: Good. ci-bot queued a 24h stress on gpu-pool-2 (longctx stress + random sharding) — job id 5467890140.

ci-bot: Job queued: gpu-pool-2/longctx-stress-5467890140. ETA results 24h.

Anita: Next steps proposed:
- create a small unit test that reproduces the index wrap at 16,384 boundary (preferably deterministic)
- apply padding fix in runtime and run quick smoke on dev
- run full AB eval (1k goldset) once smoke passes

Sasha: I'll own the unit test + failing-case artifact. Maya/Liam please iterate on runtime patch. Anita will re-run the goldset eval when we have a passing smoke. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Maya: noted, starting with a targeted repro harness now. Will post logs/heap profiles when ready.

Liam: If anyone needs immediate rollback for prod Dedicated, we should pin to magnet-14b-fp16 for affected routes. I'll prepare the rollback playbook.

Sasha: Filing follow-up ticket and linking logs: https://internal-redwood/issues/ML-2237 — add any traces there.
